business_problem: MAPFRE needed a database platform that would let its teams modernize and adapt customer and employee applications quickly without the ORM friction, schema rigidity, and redeployment risk that came with relational databases.
solution_summary: MAPFRE standardized a broad set of customer-facing and internal applications on MongoDB Atlas so development teams could work with JSON documents natively instead of forcing object-relational mappings onto application data. Atlas became a shared data platform for services such as claims, medical appointments, roadside assistance, financial management, and public-interest apps run by Fundación MAPFRE, allowing teams to reuse one flexible database across many different use cases. The company takes advantage of Atlas features such as geospatial queries, free-text search, object storage, graph capabilities, horizontal and vertical scaling, and read scaling through replica nodes that isolate reporting workloads from transactional traffic. This lets developers evolve schemas without outage-prone redeployments, support region-specific requirements across a multinational footprint, and keep critical apps responsive while new features are introduced.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the shared document database platform behind MAPFRE's customer, employee, and nonprofit applications.

data_flow: Customer actions, geolocation events, reports, and application records are stored directly as JSON in MongoDB Atlas, operational apps query the primary nodes, and reporting workloads are redirected to replica nodes so user-facing performance is preserved while teams analyze and adapt the services.
business_outcome: MAPFRE improved developer productivity, simplified application maintenance, and gained the agility to launch and modernize apps more quickly while preserving a responsive customer experience across its global operations.
metrics: MAPFRE has offices in more than 47 countries.
architecture_clues: MAPFRE uses read scaling by replicating datasets to separate nodes for reports.
Geospatial queries support location-aware services such as emergency assistance.
The platform is designed to remain cloud agnostic so MAPFRE can satisfy regional data requirements.
evidence_quotes: “MongoDB Atlas means we don’t need to create a separate database for each use case.”
“Relational databases use tables, but our developers work with JSON objects.”
“We also use read scaling to speed up queries.”
“MongoDB Atlas has opened up more opportunities and given us a competitive edge.”
